newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New government sworn in in Kabila's Congo.
newsitem.headline: New government sworn in in Kabila's Congo.

text.p: Ministers in President Laurent Kabila's new government took their oath of office on Tuesday in the Democratic Republic of the Congo capital Kinshasa, each of them clutching the new national flag.
The ministers swore the oath in the long neglected and now refurbished riverside nation palace, the old parliament building, in front of Kabila, who is also defence minister.

"I swear allegiance to the President of the Republic, obedience to the transition authority and to the laws of the Democratic Republic of the Congo," the ministers said one after the other. State television said they numbered 23.
Kabila put an end to the 32-year rule of dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May after a seven-month rebellion, proclaimed himself president with sweeping powers and banned political activity.
Opposition leader Joseph Olenghankoy said on Tuesday there was no difference between Mobutu and Kabila. "Mobutu was against freedom of expression. So is Kabila," he told reporters.

The "nation palace" served as a parliamentary building until Mobutu introduced political reform in 1990. The "people's palace" in another part of town was the seat for the transitional legislature until Kabila dissolved it.
Kabila has set up his presidential office in the nation palace building. He declined to work in Mobutu's presidential office in the hills.
